question: What security contract should OpenClaw expose for skill permission manifests: audit-only declarations, enforced grants, or a staged path that explicitly separates the two?
rationale: This defines public trust, consent, signing, and authorization semantics for third-party skills, and current code only has adjacent hooks and ClawHub trust checks rather than a settled manifest contract.

options.title: Design one core contract first
options.body: Approve a versioned schema, declared-versus-enforced semantics, ClawHub trust roots, and install/update UX before accepting partial implementations.

options.title: Accept an audit-only first slice
options.body: Allow a narrow inspect/status/policy metadata slice such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95220 only if docs prominently state it does not enforce permissions.

options.title: Keep it outside core for now
options.body: Defer core changes and ask ClawHub/plugins to continue experimenting until maintainers confirm a missing core or plugin-API seam.

recommendation.title: Design one core contract first
recommendation.body: Approve a versioned schema, declared-versus-enforced semantics, ClawHub trust roots, and install/update UX before accepting partial implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and file history point to steipete for the skills CLI, ClawHub install, dangerous-skill hardening, and prior product/security review on this exact item.
